$LUNC support is KEY right now

Hold support, $0.00007 becomes the first level to watch

Break higher with volume, $0.00012 comes into focus

This week could be important for $LUNC

The Fed finally did it — the first rate hike in three years.
And the bigger problem is the dot plot: it suggests another hike later this year is still very much on the table.

Short term, though, the market had already priced in this move and sold off ahead of the decision. That means traders can partially interpret today’s hike as “sell the rumor, buy the fact.” Bitcoin has already started to bounce a little.

But the longer-term pressure is still there. Higher rates mean tighter liquidity, stronger yields, and a tougher environment for risk assets.
That said, I’m not convinced the Fed will actually deliver the second hike.

There’s still room for the macro picture to change. If geopolitical tensions cool over the next few months, oil prices could fall, inflation could ease, and the Fed may decide that another hike is no longer necessary.

So my view is simple:
Short term: relief bounce is possible.
Medium term: rate pressure remains.
Second hike: still uncertain — it may end up being more of a warning to markets than an actual move.

For $BTC , the next major catalyst may not be today’s hike — it’s whether that second hike ever happens.

🚨 XRP Sank 10%. But CLARITY Was Only the Trigger.

XRP fell from around $1.42 to $1.26–1.30.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin fell roughly 3%.

So why did XRP get hit so much harder? 👀

The obvious answer:

The CLARITY Act.

The Senate vote ended 49–50, below the 60 votes needed to advance the bill.

That triggered disappointment — and then leverage made it worse.

Around $40M of XRP derivatives positions were liquidated, with longs accounting for more than 95%.

But the bigger shock came next.

🏦 The Fed actually raised rates.

On Sept. 16, the Fed increased the policy rate by 25 bps to 3.75–4.00% — the first hike since July 2023.

And the decision was unanimous.

Even more important:

16 of 18 policymakers projected at least one more hike in 2026.

📈 Meanwhile, the 10-year Treasury yield pushed toward 5%.

That changes the entire market backdrop.

Higher yields → higher opportunity cost → tighter financial conditions → more pressure on risk assets.

And XRP, already hit by a crypto-specific regulatory shock, suddenly had a much bigger macro problem.

But here's the twist. 👀

XRP ETF flows remained positive during the selloff.

So price weakness doesn't automatically mean institutional demand disappeared.

It may instead reflect the collision between:

ETF demand + forced liquidation + macro tightening.

And one more misconception:

CLARITY isn't an XRP-specific law.

Its failure does not automatically erase XRP's existing legal history.

🧠 Square Insight

CLARITY triggered the selloff. The Fed changed the regime.

The real test now isn't simply whether XRP can bounce.

It's whether ETF demand can absorb selling pressure while yields remain near 5% and monetary policy stays restrictive.

What matters more for XRP from here: ETF flows or the Fed?
